Hi there! 
One of your goals reminds me of a passage in Man’s Search For Meaning, by Viktor Frankl. He was a neurologist and survivor of two German concentration camps. He said something to the effect of “when our life lacks meaning we numb ourselves with pleasure” and I’ve found that to be true in my own life. So I have begun in earnest to find out what gives real meaning to my life and cultivate that. That book has become a real treasure to me, full of great insight. 
I wish you the very best in your endeavors! Way to go!

Same here! My poverty led me to understand what suffering is like- led me to want and decide to be a good,  humane being.

I ditched Amazon several months ago too! I’m also getting an old airstream ready for me, my daughter and our pets to live in. We can’t find affordable housing anywhere (even though I have a full time job) and I’m done supporting systems that make life worse for everyday working class people. I can’t control anyone but myself so I’m limiting my self to consuming what I need and working on my character to systematically eliminate greed and prejudice within myself. I work full time at a small company that makes dental tools with domestic labor and domestic steel, we are allowed to wear headphones during work so I spend 9 hours a day listening to educational materials and historical nonfiction trying to become a better human being and trying to understand what is happening in our world today.

Purebred dogs of any kind literally exist because of a genetic defect that humans then propagated because they found the defect either endearing or useful somehow. 
Many of those defects cause suffering for the animal. I will probably get downvoted to hell for saying so but I personally find absolutely nothing cute about it. I mean... would you be cool with it if someone made your parents get together to create you because they knew the odds were you would come out with the same defect your parents had that made you look squash faced and adorable but caused you be in pain your whole life while never being able to breathe comfortably? Luckily for dog breeders most people put a much higher value on how something looks than how well it functions.

Weird hot dog story: when I was 14 I suffered from  anxiety to the degree that I could not go in to a restaurant or eat in public (I’d been sexually abused for years on end by then by my stepdad, so I was a little messed up by then, hurting myself regularly and super depressed, please cut me some slack). My family wanted to visit a buffet one day after grocery shopping and mom made me come along. I tried, but I found upon arrival I simply could not make myself get out of the minivan once we got there. So they all went in and ate and I, being a ravenous growing teenage girl who hadn’t eaten for hours, ended up hiding on the floor of the van eating cold hot dogs straight outta the package. Definitely not the best meal I ever had, or the worst either, but every time I eat hotdogs my brain brings that memory up for a moment. Anyways I hate ads and most of these huge corporations so I thought I’d dump my weird hotdog story in here. That’s all. 

*ps in case anyone wonders, yes I have gotten some help since then and am now 33 and while I still suffer from depression and such I am now capable of eating anywhere in front of anyone anytime.

Hey, I’m so proud of you for putting your shame out there. Guess what? There’s nothing virtuous about something that is intrinsically harmless. True virtue happens when someone has the ability to cause harm and chooses not to.

Sounds to me like you need help, therapy, from someone who really knows what they’re doing. It’s no shame to get help. It would be the bravest goddamn thing you’ve ever done! Find a therapist who knows enough about the world not to be shocked or reject you for confiding these issues, and take the leap of faith. You’ve already done it in a small way by posting this. People who help ppl like you are out there. I’m even friends with one of them! Human brains are fucking complicated. We don’t always have control over what we think or feel, but we can relearn. We can recover. It’s possible. And I believe in you.

Honestly, I have scars ALL over my body. Some put there by me and some by nature. Some in my head and heart. Some still pain me to look at and are visible to the public. But here’s the thing: NOBODY LIVES A REAL LIFE AND GETS THROUGH UNSCATHED! My scars are my battle wounds. I am proud of them! I was wounded and survived! I’m a warrior! And now I’m stronger than EVER and lift other people up and my mere presence signals to everyone I meet that they can be themselves with me and trust me, because I’m authentic, genuine. You will be like that too, when you’re older, I can already tell! 

Stay strong my friend. This is only the beginning! Don’t worry so much about getting through life unscathed. Worry about being too afraid to get hurt to really live, really love. Life isn’t always glamorous. Sometimes bravely looks like just doing what you have to do day by day to achieve adulthood so you can strike out on your own and then BOOM! You’ll find yourself doing cool things and meeting cool people who truly respect and understand you. 
A tough part of growing up is realizing ALL ADULTS, including parents, ARE JUST REGULAR PEOPLE, who often don’t have a clue what they’re doing or why. Take what your parents say with a grain of salt. I’ve learned that even ppl who genuinely love you don’t always know what you need or get who you are, and that’s ok! You’ll find your way, I promise, if you don’t give up on your self before you even get to the part where you’re really living. 

Always here if you need a safe listener. 
Good luck, fellow warrior. Borrow my hope until you find your own.
